title: Fix the Function That Can't Modify the Caller's Variable
description: The program should double a variable's value using a helper function.
expectedBehavior: After calling doubleValue(x), x should be 10.
actualProblem: C passes arguments by value by default, so n inside doubleValue is a separate copy of x. Modifying n has no effect on the original x in main, which still prints 5.
explanation: To let a function modify a caller's variable, the function must receive a pointer to it (its address) and dereference that pointer to read or write the original value, rather than receiving a copy.
